# Phase Two — Gevurah Critique: 24 Improvements

The Awtsmoos gives boundless light a measured gate; Awtsmoos.com tests each bright idea against runtime fate.

1. Do not create a fourth movie core; converge the three already present.
2. Prefer the richer seconds-based `apps/shared/movie` only after current import/runtime tests confirm it.
3. Add Video Editor and Mitzvah Studio to canonical capabilities.
4. Model app strengths separately from shared semantic support so unified does not mean fake parity.
5. Give every adapter a projection report so unsupported data is never silently discarded.
6. Keep canonical public timing in seconds and translate milliseconds only at adapter boundaries.
7. Validate layer duration against scene duration, not merely layer start.
8. Validate keyframe ranges and channels so AI-authored motion cannot fail silently.
9. Validate identity scope clearly and reject duplicate IDs where ambiguity would break editing.
10. Preserve cast and asset references with stable IDs.
11. Include audio/dialogue/media semantics where native editors already support them.
12. Do not claim natural-language AI understanding without a model provider; expose truthful structured intent plus JSON contract.
13. Let an injected AI callback compile free-form prompts when one is actually available.
14. Keep mobile controls thumb-reachable, safe-area aware and large enough to touch.
15. Make every ten-second proof scene visibly distinct rather than metadata-only.
16. Vary cameras, transitions, charts, particles, characters, shapes and worlds across the proof.
17. Render acceptance media at an efficient profile such as 640x360/12fps while keeping production APIs resolution-independent.
18. Measure final media duration with ffprobe rather than inferring it from requested frames.
19. Capture distant frame hashes/screenshots to prove the movie is not one repeated frame.
20. Avoid rewriting Animator's heavily active command, camera, character and mobile internals unless unavoidable.
21. Hash-gate every existing shared-file rewrite because peers are writing concurrently.
22. Run syntax and module-import checks before browser tests.
23. Preserve compatibility with prototype cores through translators/re-exports rather than destructive deletion during active work.
24. After verification, reread every touched source and resolve planned-versus-actual delta before completion.
